conflicts.point: Whether shifting enforcement from upstream weight distribution to downstream market-entry gates and provenance manifests provides effective security oversight without entrenching regulatory capture.

positions.stance: Conditioning domestic market access on cryptographically verifiable provenance manifests establishes a viable legal chokepoint that manages deployment risks without relying on upstream file-sharing enforcement.
Market-entry provenance manifests fail when code executes locally via decentralized peer-to-peer networks and merely recreate corporate compliance moats that disadvantage smaller developers.

conflicts.point: Whether the operational friction and compliance overhead of export controls are justified by the need to maintain institutional recall capacity for high-consequence autonomous systems.

positions.stance: Bureaucratic and administrative friction is a tolerable price to pay for maintaining institutional oversight and mitigating irreversible catastrophic tail-risks from unconstrained cognitive capabilities.
Export licensing backlogs impose immediate, measurable human costs by delaying medical diagnostic tooling, making speculative risk mitigation an unacceptable moral failure.

verdicts.conflict: Whether shifting enforcement from upstream weight distribution to downstream market-entry gates and provenance manifests provides effective security oversight without entrenching regulatory capture.
verdicts.rationale: The skeptic position provides concrete technical constraints by noting that peer-to-peer execution bypasses market-entry gates. The safetyist position relies on theoretical compliance mechanisms without solving the core decentralized distribution problem.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Demonstrating a verifiable cryptographic protocol that halts local peer execution without central server validation would flip this verdict.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the operational friction and compliance overhead of export controls are justified by the need to maintain institutional recall capacity for high-consequence autonomous systems.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist position cites the specific fifty-dollar compute threshold required to strip post-training safety filters. This concrete metric demonstrates that static licensing mandates are rendered obsolete by rapid fine-tuning capabilities.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence that fine-tuning cannot reliably strip core safety guardrails below a much higher financial and computational threshold would change this assessment.
